Telemin Performance fizzles. Abdullah's own Veil of Summer does nothing to save it.

Resolution order (last on the stack resolves first, per [117.7]):

1. **Abdullah's Veil of Summer resolves.** Abdullah does *not* draw a card, because the only spell an opponent has cast this turn is Nico's Veil of Summer, which is green, not blue or black. Abdullah's spells can't be countered this turn, and Abdullah plus Abdullah's permanents gain hexproof from blue and from black. None of that touches Nico's Veil of Summer, which is a green spell Nico controls targeting nothing — Abdullah's Veil of Summer cannot stop it.

2. **Nico's Veil of Summer resolves.** Nico draws a card, since Abdullah cast Telemin Performance (a blue spell) this turn. Nico and Nico's permanents gain hexproof from blue and from black until end of turn.

3. **Telemin Performance tries to resolve.** Its only target is Nico, and Nico now has hexproof from blue. "Hexproof from [quality]" means the object can't be the target of spells of that quality your opponents control or abilities your opponents control from such sources ([702.11d]); note that Veil of Summer's own text explicitly grants this to *you* (the player) as well as your permanents, which is broader than the permanent-only wording in [702.11d] — the card text governs. Telemin Performance is a blue spell controlled by Nico's opponent, so Nico is now an illegal target. Since every instance of "target" on Telemin Performance is illegal, it doesn't resolve; it's removed from the stack and put into Abdullah's graveyard ([608.2b]). Nico reveals nothing, mills nothing, and Abdullah steals no creature ([Telemin Performance ruling #0] would only matter if it had resolved).

This is the same principle as [Veil of Summer ruling #0], where hexproof/anti-counter effects operate independently of whether a spell targets legally. Also, Veil of Summer has no effect until it resolves ([Veil of Summer ruling #2]), so Nico's copy still resolving in time is what matters here.

Two players vs. multiplayer: the outcome for Telemin Performance is identical. The only difference at a bigger table is the draw clauses — if some other opponent of Abdullah's had already cast a blue or black spell this turn, Abdullah's Veil of Summer would draw Abdullah a card; and Nico draws only one card no matter how many blue or black spells Nico's opponents cast ([Veil of Summer ruling #1]).
